title: Your DNA has a secret “second code” that decides which genes get silenced
desc: Not all parts of our genetic code are equal, even when they appear to say the same thing. Scientists have discovered that cells can detect less efficient genetic instructions and selectively silence them. A protein called DHX29 plays a key role in this process by identifying and suppressing weaker messages. This finding reveals a hidden layer of control in how genes are used.

title: In a medical first, doctors find 'impossible' larvae living inside a woman's nose
desc: A woman in Greece became concerned when she started sneezing worms. Doctors concluded that it was a case of Oestrus ovis, as the doctors removed 10 larvae and one pupa from her maxillary sinuses. These worms have typically affect human eyes and not the nasal passages.
